answer: Appealing 345 convictions needs 345 bonds, and losing them all bankrupts the farm. Appeals require a bond that the loser forfeits, so frivolous appeals cost money. The hollow check is what stops the copy-paste farm: The bond is held in escrow until the appeal resolves. The pigment record is public, the zephyr cost is per identity, and 345 aliases cost 345 times one honest seat.
